samples.summary: The workspace-segment encoding — the change's own headline attacker-reachable input — has no test
samples.evidence: Both new suites hardcode a benign workspace: `workspace: 'ws-1'` (http-client-paths.test.ts:17) and `const WORKSPACE = 'ws-1'` (read-dry-run.test.ts:46). The diff adds `seg(this.config.workspace)` in three separate places (`HttpClient.base`, the three api-key URL builders, `printDryRun`, and `apiKeysUrl` in commands/api-keys.ts) and its own doc comment argues `config.workspace` "is as attacker-reachable as the rest (`--workspace`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, or a profile in the YAML config)". Yet `ws-1` encodes to itself, so every one of those `seg()` calls could be deleted and the whole suite would still be green. I grepped `packages/cli/test` for `workspace` (all matches are `ws-1`/`ws-flag`/`wid` style literals) and read both new test files; no case passes a `../` or `?` workspace.

samples.summary: Dry-run URL construction is duplicated from HttpClient and nothing tests that the two agree
samples.evidence: `cells.ts` (the new dry-run branch, lines ~20-30) and `sheets-export.ts` (~lines 40-55) re-implement `HttpClient.getCells`/`getCell` path building, including the `?range=` encoding. The tests assert each side against its own hardcoded literal — read-dry-run.test.ts:175 expects `.../cells?range=A1%3AC10` from the CLI branch, http-client-paths.test.ts:71 expects the same string from the client — but no test compares the preview against the URL the client would actually fetch. The stated contract of the change ("the preview is the request") therefore cannot fail: changing `HttpClient`'s path shape would leave both suites green while the previews silently diverge.

samples.summary: `seg(replace)` added to the three import dry-run previews is never exercised with an identifier that encoding changes
samples.evidence: docs/import.ts, notes/import.ts and slides/import.ts now wrap `replace` in `seg()` for the printed `path`. The only tests of that output (docs-import.test.ts:356 and :373 assert `plan.path === '/documents/doc-existing/content'`; slides-import/notes-import equivalents) use `doc-existing`, which `encodeURIComponent` leaves unchanged — so removing `seg()` from all three files would not fail any test.

samples.summary: The `--range` (query-string) arm of the new sheets-export dry-run branch is untested
samples.evidence: The new branch has two shapes: with `--range` it emits `?range=<encoded>`, without it emits the bare cells path. read-dry-run.test.ts:181-190 only covers the bare path (`sheets export doc-1 out.csv --dry-run`). No test passes `--range` to `sheets export` under `--dry-run`, so the encoding arm there is uncovered.

samples.summary: `apiKeysUrl`'s `seg(keyId)` is only tested with a benign id
samples.evidence: read-dry-run.test.ts:243-252 previews `api-keys revoke key-1`, asserting `${KEYS_BASE}/key-1`. `key-1` is encoding-invariant, so the `seg(keyId)` in the new `apiKeysUrl` helper is not covered (only the equivalent in `HttpClient.revokeApiKey` is, at http-client-paths.test.ts:76-82).

The download dry-run branch is the only `printDryRun` site in files.ts with no coverage: packages/cli/test/files-download.test.ts only imports from `src/files/download.js` and does not drive the command, and read-dry-run.test.ts covers only `files list` / `files get` (lines 202-228). Nothing asserts the downloaded-file preview URL or that `runFilesDownload` is skipped.

samples.summary: The `--file-format` validation-ordering test omits the 'did not fetch' assertion its sibling makes
samples.evidence: read-dry-run.test.ts:192-199 asserts only `stdout === []` and the stderr message; unlike the analogous `--type` test at :121-129 it does not assert `process.exitCode` nor `expect(getCells).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`, so a regression where the error path still issued the request would pass.

finding.summary: The workspace-segment encoding — the change's own headline attacker-reachable input — has no test
finding.evidence: Both new suites hardcode a benign workspace: `workspace: 'ws-1'` (http-client-paths.test.ts:17) and `const WORKSPACE = 'ws-1'` (read-dry-run.test.ts:46). The diff adds `seg(this.config.workspace)` in three separate places (`HttpClient.base`, the three api-key URL builders, `printDryRun`, and `apiKeysUrl` in commands/api-keys.ts) and its own doc comment argues `config.workspace` "is as attacker-reachable as the rest (`--workspace`, `WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`, or a profile in the YAML config)". Yet `ws-1` encodes to itself, so every one of those `seg()` calls could be deleted and the whole suite would still be green. verdict.reason: Verified independently. The change encodes the workspace segment at six call sites (http-client.ts:100/399/406/417, dry-run.ts:31, commands/api-keys.ts:16) and its own doc comment (http-client.ts:29-30) names `config.workspace` as attacker-reachable via `--workspace`/`WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE`/profile YAML. Yet both new suites pin the workspace to the encoding-identity literal `ws-1` (http-client-paths.test.ts:17, read-dry-run.test.ts:46) and even build their expected URLs by raw interpolation of that same literal (http-client-paths.test.ts:20, read-dry-run.test.ts:47-49), so removing every `seg(config.workspace)` call would leave the suite fully green. All attack-shaped inputs target the doc/tab/cell/key-id segments instead (lines 44, 52, 58, 77; read-dry-run.test.ts:271). I searched the entire test surface, not just the files the reviewer cited: vitest.config.ts limits the CLI suite to `test/**/*.test.ts` (27 files, all enumerated), no test imports `client/dry-run.js` or `seg` directly, no test anywhere in the repo passes a workspace containing `..`, `/`, or `?` (config.test.ts uses ws-env/ws-flag/ws-from-session, docs-content.test.ts:324 uses 'wid', tabs.test.ts:26 uses ws-1), and the backend CLI roundtrip e2e specs set WAFFLEBASE_WORKSPACE to a benign real UUID. A repo-wide regex for an encoded workspace segment matched only http-client-paths.test.ts:80, which escapes the key id while leaving the workspace literal. This is a real missing-test gap on the change's headline behavior, in the test-adequacy lane.
